candidates.statement: Payment service returns 503 on POST /v1/authorizations, which order propagates as 502 on /v1/orders and gateway surfaces as 502 on /v1/checkout. Traces show the failing hop is payment (503), not inventory (200) or redis.
candidates.uncertainty: Payment-side logs/metrics excluded (gw_logs unavailable); root cause within payment (config, saturation) not established.

report.explanation: Checkout 502s trace to payment returning 503 on /v1/authorizations; order propagates 502. Inventory/redis succeed. Bounded to payment-side failure, but the specific mechanism needs payment telemetry (gw_logs excluded).
missing_evidence: Payment service logs and metrics for /v1/authorizations to determine why it returns 503
Payment dependency health (postgresql) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency at payment
